title.value: Recovery after stroke: the severely impaired are a distinct group
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Recovery after stroke: the severely impaired are a distinct group

analysis.description: The paper discusses the distinct recovery patterns of severely and non-severely impaired stroke patients by employing Bayesian hierarchical models. It aims to provide evidence that severely impaired patients have different recovery trajectories compared to non-severely impaired patients and assesses the validity of the severe versus non-severe separation in recovery modelling.

type.justification: The paper involves data analysis from eight patient cohorts, uses Bayesian hierarchical models, and evaluates prediction performance, indicating it is an empirical study.
type.quote:
Methods
We designed a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate three-to-six-months upper limb Fugl- Meyer(FM) scores after stroke.

name.justification: The study focuses on motor recovery after stroke, which is a key area of neuroscience research, particularly related to neurorehabilitation.
name.quote:
Introduction
Stroke causes different levels of impairment and the degree of recovery varies greatly between patients.

name.justification: The paper employs Bayesian hierarchical models to analyze recovery patterns in stroke patients.
name.quote:
Methods
We designed a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate three-to-six-months upper limb Fugl- Meyer(FM) scores after stroke.

name.justification: The study aims to analyze recovery patterns and improve clinical decision-making and neurorehabilitation treatments based on different levels of stroke impairment.
name.quote:
Introduction
A comprehensive and more mechanistic understanding of recovery after stroke is thus indispensable to successfully guide clinical decision-making and neurorehabilitation treatments.

name.justification: The paper introduces and employs Bayesian hierarchical models to assess stroke recovery patterns, thus it is the main model discussed.
name.quote:
Methods
We designed a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate three-to-six-months upper limb Fugl- Meyer(FM) scores after stroke.

is_contributed.justification: The Bayesian hierarchical model is specifically designed and implemented by the authors to study stroke recovery patterns.
is_contributed.quote:
Methods
We designed a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate three-to-six-months upper limb Fugl- Meyer(FM) scores after stroke.

is_executed.justification: The model is applied to patient data to estimate FM scores and predict recovery patterns.
is_executed.quote: We designed a Bayesian hierarchical model...Finally, we estimated the out-of-sample prediction performance for patients across the entire initial impairment range.

is_compared.justification: The paper compares various models with different sub-group categorizations to find the best one for recovery pattern analysis.
is_compared.quote:
Methods
We performed Bayesian model comparisons to evaluate whether recovery pattern differed between severely and non-severely affected patients.
